newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firm, seen higher.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firm, seen higher.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended higher on Tuesday as the market remained largely unmoved by news that a major Japanese firm was being investigated for suspected links with racketeers.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract ended up 170 points at 18,225 after hitting a high of 18,290.
The reports about Ajinomoto Co came on the back of Nomura Securities' disclosure on March 6 that two of its directors had been involved in suspected illegal deals.
"All this news is part and parcel of past Tokyo activities," said a senior trader with an Asian institution.
He said the market was likely to be fairly subdued ahead of the Japanese financial year end on March 31 and the Bank of Japan's quarterly business sentiment survey on April 2.
"In the short-term I wouldn't expect much, although the New York market is bullish," he added.
A chartist with a local futures house said the March Nikkei showed more of an upside bias but was likely to face resistance around 18,360 and a stronger barrier at 18,455.
He said a break below 18,120 could push it through the 18,000 level, but added very strong support would emerge around 17,800 as the market had already failed to breach that level twice.
The March MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 349.6 against its opening 347.0 on volume of 450 lots. April was at 346.0 against 343.5 on 502 lots.
